question:
A 56-year-old woman visits her gynecologist for a routine examination and reports no symptoms. She
has no medical history, uses a copper IUD for contraception, and has no family history of cancer. Her
vital signs are within normal limits. Breast examination reveals a 1-cm smooth, nontender, mobile mass
in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast. The skin and nipples appear normal, and there is no
axillary lymphadenopathy. Breast ultrasound shows an oval-shaped lesion with posterior acoustic
enhancement, 0.40 mm thick walls, and internal echoes without solid components. A mammogram is
unremarkable. What is the most appropriate next step in managing this patient? Answer Choices: (A)
Observation with annual follow-up only (B) Fine-needle aspiration with cytology (C) Mammogram in six
months (D) Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (E) Ultrasound-guided aspiration (F) MRI of the
breast (G) Referral to a breast surgeon for evaluation (H) Repeat mammogram and ultrasound in three
months (I) Excisional biopsy (J) Clinical breast exam and breast ultrasound in six months
 A. Referral to a breast surgeon for evaluation
B. Repeat mammogram and ultrasound in three months
C. Mammogram in six months
D. Excisional biopsy
E. Observation with annual follow-up only
F. Clinical breast exam and breast ultrasound in six months
G. Fine-needle aspiration with cytology
H. MRI of the breast
I. Ultrasound-guided aspiration

J. Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy
